Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our pricing and standard terms for your requirements.

For this item, we can offer a price of €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To give you some background on our current cost structure, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.

We value our business relationship and look forward to serving you from our extensive product range.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.subject: 1.4404 bar – proposal for a longer supply agreement
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining the movements in your cost components. I appreciate the transparency. Those annual movements are useful context; your own order history for this part is also a practical reference for the price discussion. Please see the supporting figures below.

Our annual requirement is 23700 kg. I have attached the shared forecast so that you can assess the demand profile alongside the proposed agreement.

We propose EUR 5.07 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a contract term of 24 months, without a price adjustment clause. This retains the fixed-price structure of your offer while giving the relationship a longer contractual basis.

Please review the price on that basis, taking the documented order history and the annual requirement together. I would welcome your view on this package.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

move.subject: Re: Bar pricing and contract terms
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for checking the alloy data and reflecting it in your revised offer. I also appreciate your continued agreement to payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract.

I understand that you still require an AS-14404 clause and that you are not sharing a further breakdown of your calculation. I am not asking for confidential detail. However, the recent movement in PPI-C2431 is also relevant to the base price, since you identified it as a main cost driver. Please see the verified figures below alongside the annual movements you cited.

We can move our proposal to EUR 5.18 per kg, with payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract, without a price adjustment clause. I recognise that the fixed-price structure remains a point of disagreement; please have your pricing committee review this revised package against the additional market evidence rather than treating that point as settled.

Please let me know what price and structure the committee can approve on this basis.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

move.subject: Revised fixed-price package for committee review
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for verifying the producer-price data and reflecting it in your revised offer. I appreciate your movement and your continued agreement to payment at 90 days net over a 24-month term.

I note that both of your packages retain an AS-14404 clause and that you regard a fixed price as unfeasible. The price structure remains the point we need to resolve; there is no need to revisit the evidence you have already checked.

We can increase our proposal to EUR 5.25 per kg, with payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract, without a price adjustment clause. This movement is specifically for the fixed-price structure. Please ask your pricing committee to assess the revised package as a whole and confirm whether it can approve it.

If the committee still requires indexation, I would welcome the calculation discussion you offered, focused on what prevents approval of this fixed-price package rather than confidential cost detail.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

strategy:
Supplier: Blankstahl Werdenfels (family stainless bar stockholder, inside sales desk, owner in background). Public
notes: its sales director "will focus on customers with volume"; price changes above 2 % need its pricing committee
(meets every two weeks); the owner offered to walk us through their calculation. It inserts an AS-14404 index
clause itself for long terms (do NOT propose a clause), accepts 90-day payment, and asks "Which figures is that
based on? Please send us the data." when we state things without IDs.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (35 sessions): it anchors close to OUR first ask when the ask is credible (ask 5.37 with a verified
claim -> it answered 5.40), but a deep ask (5.12 or lower) makes it answer 5.60-5.70 instead. After the first reply
it moves at most 2 % (about 0.10) per round, only when we move too, and it goes final after 2-3 steps or at once if
our sheet is unchanged or our move is upward past its price. Every past session was lost by moving UP after it had
nearly met our ask. So: ask a credible but low price in round 1 WITH its own purchase-order price as the argument,
then move up only in tiny steps (+0.02 to +0.03) staying below its price, one new verified claim each round, same
package (no clause, 90 days, 24 months), never touch payment or term.
Plan: ROUND 1 - state our fixed annual requirement (case volume) and that we commit to it bindingly for the term,
attach the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite BOTH the purchase-order claim (its own delivered price this
year for this part: the point is that its 2026 deliveries ran at that price) AND fc-latest (two claims); ONE sheet: no index clause, 90 days,
24 months at the level closest to EUR 5.10. ROUND 2 - thank it, cite the AS-14404 fall (one window), move up +0.03; if its price is
already within 0.05 of ours, move only +0.01. ROUND 3 - cite the PPI-C2431 fall, move up +0.03; ask
it to take the package to its pricing committee if the step exceeds 2 %. ROUND 4 - no new claim (never re-cite a series), +0.03.
ROUND 5 - no new claim (never re-cite a series), +0.02, ask for its best committee-approved price. Code accepts
when it agrees or goes final. Tone: warm, concrete, partner-like, short; one argument per sentence. Do not use
the scorecard claim.
